chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you want me to show you the shirt of Ali (peace be upon him) in which he was struck, and show you his blood?' I said, 'Yes'. So he called for it, and it was in a basket. He took it out and spread it, and behold, it was a shirt of Qarabis cloth, resembling Al-Sunbulani. The place of the pocket down to the ground had blood, which was white like milk, resembling a stroke of the sword. He said: 'This is the shirt of Ali (peace be upon him) in which he was struck, and this is the trace of his blood.' So I measured its body with the span, and it was three spans, and I measured its lower part with the span, and it was twelve spans.

key_terms.السُّنْبُلَانِيَّ: A type of fabric or weave pattern
key_terms.سَفَط: A basket made of woven palm leaves
key_terms.شَبَرْتُ: I measured with the span (distance from thumb to little finger)
key_terms.شُطَبِ السَّيْفِ: The stroke or mark of the sword
key_terms.كَرَابِيسَ: A type of fine cotton or linen fabric

ai.seo_question: What are the physical characteristics and dimensions of Imam Ali's shirt as described in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) presents the shirt of Imam Ali (AS) to Al-Hasan al-Sayqal, demonstrating the specific location and nature of the wound from the strike of Ibn Muljam. This physical evidence serves as a tangible verification of the historical event, emphasizing the purity of the blood (white like milk) and the precise dimensions of the cut, thereby linking the garment's material reality to the spiritual status of the Imam. The narration underscores the authenticity of the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage and their unique connection to divine authority through these preserved relics.
